Hi Brian — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, with artifacts attached: subprocessor_matrix.csv and dataflow_diagram.pdf.

1) Export controls: Redwood's hosted inference is not subject to ITAR. For EAR, we do not perform encryption export of controlled cryptographic items; our offering is SaaS inference and does not contain dual-use software classified under EAR 99 in typical model/service configurations. For procurement paperwork we can provide a short attestation: "Redwood Inference confirms that, to the best of its knowledge, the hosted inference service as delivered to Greenline Health is not subject to ITAR and is not a controlled EAR commodity under commonly deployed configurations; customer-specific usages or models that are controlled remain the responsibility of the customer." Let me know if Legal needs tighter wording.

2) Deletion proofing: We attach a representative deletion_job_log_snippet.txt. Typical proof artifacts we provide on request are: deletion job ID, timestamp, bucket/object keys (redacted if PHI), and a signed job completion entry from our scheduler. For CPRA/CCPA responses we can also supply audit-log excerpts showing the entire lifecycle for a specific identifier (started, queued, deleted). The deletion process is cumulative: data is zeroed in KV stores, indexes are dropped, and S3 objects are removed with version purge.

3) Subprocessors & flows: See subprocessor_matrix.csv for current list; the dataflow_diagram.pdf highlights edges where transient telemetry (latency metrics, truncated request hashes) may be emitted. We mark any component that stores customer-provided content as "persisting PII/PD".

If you want a signed, one-line export control attestation we can provide it on Redwood letterhead. Also happy to redline a short DPA subclause to capture deletion proof (sample language below).

Sample clause (for illustration):
"Upon Customer request, Redwood will provide evidence of deletion for Customer Personal Data processed as a Service Provider under applicable US state privacy laws in the form of deletion job identifiers, timestamps, and supporting audit-log excerpts, subject to redaction for third-party data or security-sensitive information."

If that looks reasonable I can ask Contracts to turn it into a DocuSign amendment.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessor_matrix.csv, dataflow_diagram.pdf, deletion_job_log_snippet.txt

Marissa — reviewing and confirming.

Deletion proofing: the snippet you attached is our canonical sample. Typical fields included in the artifact we share: deletion_job_id (format: del-YYYYMMDD-XXXXXXXX), initiated_by (service account id), target_identifiers (redacted), completed_at (ISO8601), completion_signature (sha256 of job manifest signed by our key id). We populate an audit-log excerpt that includes the job id, the scheduler entry, and the storage object purge events. We redact object keys to customer-provided obfuscation standard when PHI is present.

Export controls: Jonas confirms there are no ITAR components in the hosted inference stack. We don't ship hardware or controlled crypto in a way that would trigger EAR for standard models. The attestation Marissa drafted is acceptable as a procurement-level statement.

Subprocessors: current matrix is accurate; I've uploaded a "redacted sample" folder in the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bexample (read-only link for legal ops).
